author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell described what his daily life actually looks like now, staying conscious about everything he eats, says, and does so he doesn't slip into old habits without thinking. He explained his routine of regularly exposing himself to extreme heat and cold, drawing on a lesson that the moment in front of you isn't what's bothering you, you're the one bothering yourself about it. He also talked about practicing Brazilian jiu jitsu a few times a week, not because it came naturally, but because of the strange trust it builds between people, being choked to the point of tapping out, then it's simply over. Russell connected all of it to an older, more ancestral way of living, one built around touch, community, and shared physical experience rather than isolation.

title: Why Russell Lives Like A Monk Now...

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest argued that Disney got progressively taken over by what he called a woke mind virus, starting subtly with stories like Rapunzel reframed entirely around self development, with the male lead reduced to a minor detail. He said it only got worse from there, eventually reaching a point with Snow White where the political reframing became so heavy handed the film reportedly took years longer to make because the original version leaned so hard into commentary it barely resembled the story that made cultural history in the first place. He argued Disney is now trapped by its own shifting agenda, watching audiences simply stop caring, and questioned whether the studio can even recover from the damage at this point.
